newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain coup plot suspects may face death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain coup plot suspects may face death penalty.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court has begun the trial of 59 people arrested in connection with an alleged Iranian-backed attempt to topple the government and some might face death sentences if convicted, lawyers said on Sunday.
"Some suspects...accused of spying...and working to topple the government face death sentences if convicted," one lawyer told Reuters.
The lawyer, who asked not to be identified, said 81 people had been accused of taking part in the alleged plot, but only 59 would stand trial. The rest were still at large.
A Bahraini official told Reuters the trial of 59 suspects accused of attempting to overthrow the government by force began on Saturday and was continuing.
"The trial is open only for the defendants' families and their lawyers," the official said.
Bahrain in June accused Shi'ite Moslem Iran of backing an attempt to topple the government and said it had arrested around 60 people in connection with the alleged plot.

Iran denied the allegation and said it was not interfering in internal affairs of Bahrain, where members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community demanding political and economic reforms by the Sunni rulers have waged a campaign of bombings, arson attacks, sabotage and riots since December 1994.
The lawyer said the defendants had been divided into around seven groups.
"Saturday's trial of the first group has been adjourned to March 15. Others will be on trial today (Sunday)," the official said. He gave no further details.

The suspects were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain.
Firefighters on Saturday foiled an attempt to blow up a car in a Manama car park apparently to coincide with the start of the trial.
"Investigations showed there was a gas cylinder with a timer in the stolen car. Firefighters quickly brought the fire under control," a government official told Reuters.
He said there were no casualties or damage, but declined to say what had caused the fire.
It was the first reported incident of its kind in several weeks in the Bahraini capital, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested since unrest in support of demands by members of the island's majority Shi'ite community.
